findings.title: Cache is populated before DB write, so rejected devices bypass limit
findings.body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go tagDeviceUI() checks localCache, then calls SetDefault(key) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice(). If CreateOrUpdateDevice() returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the cache entry is left in place. The next request for the same new deviceId hits the early-return cache path and returns nil without touching the DB, so authentication succeeds even though the device was never persisted. The limit is therefore only enforced once per cache TTL. Fix: only Set the cache after a successful create/update, and do not cache failures.

findings.title: Count-then-insert check is not atomic and can exceed device limit
findings.body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go CreateOrUpdateDevice() does CountDevices() and if count >= deviceLimit falls back to update-only, otherwise does an upsert INSERT. The check and the insert are two separate transactions with no lock or unique-count constraint. Two concurrent requests for different new devices can both observe count < limit and both insert, overshooting the configured limit. Fix with a transaction/serializable guard, atomic insert guarded by count, or document that the limit is best-effort.

findings.title: Anonymous auth now blocks on synchronous DB write with no timeout
findings.body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go Authenticate() previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout using context.Background(), so login never waited for the DB. The PR changed it to call anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously on the request context, which does CountDevices() plus an insert/update. Every anonymous request now pays DB latency on the auth hot path, and a slow DB stalls login with no bound other than request cancellation. This is a latency/availability regression. Fix: keep enforcement but add a short timeout, fail-open on timeout/DB error, or revert to async with enforcement only where needed.

findings.title: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService breaks DI by replacing AnonStore with sqlStore
findings.body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go ProvideAnonymousDeviceService() changed its injected parameter from anonStore anonstore.AnonStore to sqlStore db.DB and now hard-codes anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit) internally. Any wire injector, enterprise override, or test that provided a custom/mock AnonStore no longer compiles or can inject a fake. It also makes the service untestable without a real DB. Fix: keep accepting AnonStore and inject the limit separately, or provide a constructor overload.
